assumptions: The same observed directed topology and unchanged SUMO vehicle/junction parameters are used in every comparison; the microscopic model is not calibrated field truth.
The six original OD release schedules are independent of the number of candidate routes. All request IDs, original release times and vehicle properties are fixed within paired groups.

A selects a same-endpoint candidate at release using current known external-edge speed costs. The default participates, ties retain default, and future event recovery or future tasks are not consulted.

B adds bounded source admission after task publication. It acts only on ordinary requests released at/after the task and not yet submitted to SUMO whose chosen path intersects the task's currently remaining corridor.

Task corridor updates use current TraCI vehicle route position; before task insertion its already assigned route is used. Each ordinary request waits at most 45 seconds at source, and task-related control expires 180 seconds after release.
Source admission authority is an explicit hypothetical governance action. All source control and SUMO insertion waiting remain charged from the unchanged original release time.
Task and ordinary vehicles share exactly one vType and the same road permissions. There is no special speed, red-light override, lane priority, repositioning or vehicle removal.
Slow-event speeds and durations are predeclared assumptions, not observed accidents or measured capacity. All profile results, including no benefit or harm, are retained.
The fixed experiment anchor maps simulation seconds to a declared wall clock only; the counterfactual traffic demand and event are not a reconstruction of the live collection window.
A fitted ETA observation layer, if supplied separately, is a statistical reference and does not identify or validate the microscopic parameters.
